newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Anglo Irish confident of further progress.
newsitem.headline: Anglo Irish confident of further progress.

text.p: Anglo Irish Bank Corp Plc said on Tuesday that it was confident of further progress in the current year and of a twelfth year of increased profit.
"The economic indicators are very good for the next year with low inflation and low interest rates which should generate strong loan demand," the bank said in its full-year results statement.
The group said it remained confident of the continued growth potential of its business despite the challenges posed by Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"While the pace of development of financial services continues to quicken and rationalisation becomes the dominant trend, the market in which the bank operates will continue to demand the independence, service and flexibility which it delivers so successfully to customers," it said.
Earlier, Anglo Irish announced a 26 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 24.1 million punts for the year ended September 30, 1996.
Advances rose by 36 percent to 1.46 billion Irish pounds while deposits grew by 30 percent to 2.08 billion with growth coming largely from retail deposits.

"The Irish and United Kingdom lending markets have been very buoyant during the year. Due to competition there has been some pressure on margins but we have continued our policy of being selective in granting credit," the bank said.
It said all sections of the bank contributed to profits with the Irish contribution rising by 18 percent to 18.1 million.

The UK, including the Isle of Man, made profits of 4.9 million, an increase of 53 percent on last year, while the bank's wholly-owned Austrian subsidiary, Anglo Irish Bank (Austria), made a contribution of 1.1 million to group profits.
The bank said it maintained tight control on costs and its cost/income ratio stood at 46 percent.

It also said its capital adequacy ratios were very strong with a total capital ratio in excess of 13 percent and said it had sufficient capital in place to sustain its targeted growth over the next five years.
